**Visual observations:**
- Soybean plant, whole-plant view
- Lower/inner leaves showing yellowing and chlorosis
- Upper canopy leaves remain mostly green
- Some leaves show possible interveinal chlorosis pattern (yellowing between veins, veins staying greener)
- No obvious discrete spots, pustules, white mycelium, or necrotic lesions visible
- Stems appear green with no obvious lesions

**Reasoning through candidates:**

- **Sudden death syndrome (SDS)**: Classic presentation is interveinal chlorosis starting on lower leaves, progressing upward, while roots/crown have Fusarium infection. Foliar symptoms match — lower leaves yellowing with veins remaining relatively green, upper leaves still green. This is the strongest match.
- **Brown Stem Rot**: Similar foliar interveinal chlorosis symptoms to SDS, but internal stem pith browning is the distinguishing feature — not visible here.
- **Soybean Dwarf Mosaic Virus / Bean Pod Mottle Virus**: Could show mottling, but no strong mosaic pattern visible.
- **Green stem disorder**: Plants retain green stems while pods/leaves die — doesn't match well here.
- **Phytophthora / Pythium**: More of damping off or stem lesion pattern.

The lower-leaf interveinal chlorosis with upper leaves remaining green is the hallmark of SDS foliar phase.
